feature: Text inside a component is drawn clean
summary: A word you type on a screenshot still gets its soft glow so it stays readable. The moment that word is inside a component, the glow stops being drawn, so the label on a button you drew looks as crisp as the app's own five. Nothing is erased: take the text back out and the glow is there again.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Needs Make a component out of what you drew, which is on by default.

try.do: Press N for a blank canvas.
Draw a rectangle, then press T and type Save on top of it.
Look closely at the word: it sits in a pale glow.
Select both, press Command G, then Option Command K and name it Save button.
Drag a copy of it off the Library shelf and compare the two.
Double click into the component, pick the label, and look at the Shadow section.
Select the component and press Shift Command G to take it apart again.

evaluate: Does the label on your button now read as crisply as the Button and Nav Bar tiles on the shelf?
Was the glow on the loose text obvious enough that its going feels like a fix rather than a change you did not ask for?
Is a component the right line to draw, or would you want the glow gone the moment text lands inside any group?
With the label picked, does Enable Shadow reading off match what you see on the canvas?
Taking the component apart brings the glow back. Is that what you expected, or would you rather it stayed gone once it went?
rough: The difference is real but quiet at window size: in the two captures it is easiest to see by zooming into the word Save.
Text typed straight onto a Frame, a screen rather than a component, still wears the glow. That is the same complaint one level up and is filed as its own task rather than widened into this one.

If you had already tuned the glow by hand before promoting, it keeps drawing inside the component, because by then it is a shadow you chose rather than the automatic one. Deliberate, but it means two labels can differ for a reason nothing on screen explains.
Screen Recording was granted for this run, so the three pictures are real captures of the probe window, not offscreen renders.
